title: Sky Governance holds the majority of SPK, making the Agent token a claim held mostly by the parent ecosystem
content:
The distribution operations in A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.2.1.2 record that the Genesis Supply was minted to an account owned by SPK Company Ltd, which then transferred 6.5 billion SPK to the **Sky Pause Proxy** (A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.2.1.2.2) and 918,760,451 SPK to the **Spark SubProxy Account** (A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.2.1.2.3), with the remainder going to the token launch and the Spark Foundation.

The individual amounts are parameters, but their ratio is a structural claim: 65% of the Agent's token sits with Sky Governance and roughly 9% with the Agent itself. Sky is not a minority strategic investor in Spark — it is the majority holder.

This is the economic counterpart to the governance limits placed on Spark elsewhere in the Artifact. Sky's willingness to supply SparkLend with liquidity below market rates and to absorb the resulting risk is rational because most of the equity-like upside from Spark's growth accrues back to Sky. The Agent model does not rely on goodwill between the ecosystem and its Agents; it aligns them by ownership.

It also explains why an emissions override held by Sky is not an outside intervention: the party that could dilute SPK holders is itself the largest SPK holder, and so bears most of the cost of using that power.
description: Of the 10 billion Genesis Supply, 6.5 billion went to the Sky Pause Proxy and only ~0.92 billion to Spark's own SubProxy — a controlling stake by construction.
